scope: Phase 2 of the shared-core plan: the Unity host over libweva. This receipt grows with the phase; each step records its gate as it lands.

windows.load_test: weva_core_load_test: abi 0.25, button at 10.0,10.0 size 29.3x22.0, 4 draws, layout probe sizes match, ok
windows.build_json: weva_core.dll.build.json stamped (library and source digests, git state, compiler, ABI 0.25)

linux.exports: 113 dynamic symbols, all weva_* (version script, local: *); a first build exported none because hidden visibility was applied to the core objects before the version script could pick them, fixed by scoping the preset to the plugin sources
linux.load_test: weva_core_load_test: abi 0.25, button at 10.0,10.0 size 29.3x22.0, 4 draws, ok (identical geometry to Windows)

step_1_plugin_build.gate: met: the DLL loads in Unity 6000.4.1f1 EditMode and weva_abi_version() reports 0.25 (Plugin_ReportsHeaderAbiVersion)

step_2_bindings.shape: blittable: unsafe pointers, nuint for size_t, fixed buffers for arrays, delegate* unmanaged[Cdecl] callback fields, Cdecl DllImport externs; nothing marshalled, so Mono and IL2CPP share the file

cases: GeneratedStruct_MatchesNativeSize x12 (weva_config, weva_vertex, weva_rounded_rect, weva_backdrop_effect, weva_draw, weva_texture, weva_render_backend, weva_glyph_bitmap, weva_font_backend, weva_shaped_glyph, weva_event, weva_binding_source)
Document_RoundTrips (create, HTML, CSS, update, focus_next, tag name, bounds 10,10, draws with triangles, destroy)

step_2_bindings.gate: met: the document round trip passes from C# in EditMode and agrees with the C++ load test

steps_open: live-scene (Game view) verification of WevaNativeDocument through UIRenderPass
colour glyph rasterization and a real shaper for the font adapter
an ABI switch to freeze animations for dumps if the oracle should cover animated pages
limitations: The Unity editor is not on the CI runners; the EditMode run and the host comparison are recorded here and must be rerun by hand after header, generator or adapter changes.
Windows x64 only in the package (Plugins/x86_64); the Linux .so builds and passes the load test but is not installed in the package.
The plugin binary is gitignored; build it with hosts/unity (README) before the Native EditMode tests can run.
The URP in-pass path composites in linear space (URP's colour buffer), so blended edges differ slightly from the gamma-composited offscreen render used for the comparison.

step_3_font_adapter.adapter: Packages/com.wevaui/Runtime/Native/UnityFontBackend.cs: weva_font_backend over FontEngine (TextCore) plus the positioned shaper; faces from Font assets, files or bytes; per-code-point fallback faces encoded in the glyph id; real bold/italic variants; @font-face rules read from the core and registered (SyncCssFontFaces) through the document asset reader
contract_ported_from_godot: face metrics scale the engine design units (FaceMetrics_ScaleTheEngineDesignUnits, BytesFace_MatchesTheAssetFace)

glyph index and unhinted glyph metrics are the engine's own at the rounded pixel size (GlyphIndex_IsTheEngineIndex, GlyphMetrics_AreTheEngineUnhintedMetrics, GlyphMetrics_RoundThePixelSizeLikeTheGodotAdapter)
coverage bitmaps: ink, top-down rows, metrics describe the bitmap, no bitmap for a space (Rasterize_*)

shaping: UTF-8 byte clusters, sizing protocol, control characters, per-code-point fallback, pair adjustment, positioned form agrees with the legacy callback, 300-glyph fallback run (Shape_*, PositionedShaper_*)
the core lays out with the adapter: a span is as wide as the adapter's advances, a registered family switches the face (Document_LaysOutWithTheAdapter)
findings: FontEngine.GetPairAdjustmentRecord(first, second) returns an uninitialised record for a pair the face does not kern and segfaulted inside TextCore::FontEngine::GetPairAdjustmentRecord on an ordinary Inter pair (crash log in .utmp/unity-test); the adapter uses GetPairAdjustmentRecords(List<uint>) per adjacent pair instead. The C# engine's UnityFontEngineBackend.TryGetKernAdvance binds GetGlyphPairAdjustmentRecord, which answers zero for every pair on 6000.4 (its kerning is silently off); not changed in this phase.

GetPairAdjustmentRecords values are design units and list a pair once per covering subtable in the font's order (Inter L-: -104 pair subtable, then -174 class subtable); the first record is what OpenType applies (-1.625px at 32px, matching fontTools). A long glyph list answered the same pair class-first, so the query is per pair.

UnmanagedCallersOnlyAttribute is not in Unity 6000.4's class library (netstandard 2.1 / mono profiles checked); callbacks use MonoPInvokeCallback delegates cast to the generated function-pointer fields.
LoadFontFace overloads with an int take a point size, not a face index; font collections are not supported by the adapter.
limitations: no ligatures or mark positioning (one glyph per code point plus pair kerning)
colour glyphs are not rasterized (COLOR render mode not wired)
FontEngine is process-global: the adapter reloads its face after any other user (before every update)
step_3_font_adapter.gate: met: 19 UnityFontBackend EditMode checks pass (part of the 42/42 Native run below)

step_4_render_adapter.adapter: Packages/com.wevaui/Runtime/Native/NativeDocumentRenderer.cs + Resources/Weva-NativeMesh.shader + WevaNativeDocument (MonoBehaviour, IUINativePaintSource drawn by UIRenderPass); textures mirrored by id, consecutive same-texture draws merged into one mesh, backdrop-filter draws skipped, colour composited in gamma space like the Godot host (core colours are linear, texels sRGB)

comparison_with_godot.method: godot-port/hosts/unity/compare_hosts.py (compare_render.py metric) on 1280x720 renders of the same html/css with the same font bytes (@font-face Inter); Godot via capture.tscn (opengl3, 4.7.1 + build222 extension), Unity via the Parity EditMode test; images and diff maps in .utmp/parity/<page>/
comparison_with_godot.gate_default: compare_render.py gates at 1.0% structural; both pages sit just above it (1.08%, 1.01%) and are NOT claimed to pass that number
differences_explained: text: every glyph edge differs (the diff maps are the page's text) because the two hosts rasterize with different engines (FontEngine SMOOTH vs TextServer) and position differently (TextServer quarter-pixel advances vs FontEngine fractional advances); layout geometry is identical (same core, same font bytes)
colour emoji icons in randhtml are blank on Unity (colour glyphs not rasterized yet), the largest single structural cluster there
1px lines and rounded-rect edges (button borders, bar underlines) differ by one row where the two rasterizers round differently

the first render had a colour-space bug (vertex colours converted to linear twice, blending in linear space): mean delta 28/255, 72% over tolerance; fixed by following the Godot host (encode the core's linear colours to sRGB, blend in gamma space into a raw target)

step_4_render_adapter.gate: met with explained differences: the Frontier Camp page and the randhtml demo render through the core in Unity and agree with the Godot host everywhere but on text rasterization and colour glyphs

step_5_input_events.adapter: NativeDocument interaction calls (pointer with buttons/modifiers, key edges, text input, paste, wheel scroll, focus stepping, IME composition, caret bounds, select-all/undo/redo) and PollEvents into NativeEvent; NativeInputFeed reads the Input System with the Godot host rules (a Space the button took is not also text; Ctrl shortcuts route to selection/clipboard/history; the feed reports whether the document consumed the input); WevaNativeDocument exposes the Godot addon signals as C# events
step_5_input_events.ported_from_godot: the document-level checks of keyboard_integration_tests.gd and input_integration_tests.gd (Enter activates on key-down and repeats, Space on release and not as text, focus loss cancels a held button, checkbox/radio/slider/details/popover keyboard behaviour, implicit submission and a disabled default button, Unicode typing, Backspace and paste, pointer down/up/click/enter/leave, release elsewhere is no click, secondary button is a context menu, pointer-events:none passes hit testing, wheel scroll at a point with clamping, IME composition and caret, tab order with and without wrap); the checks about Godot Control routing (overlays, CanvasLayer, native focus chain) are not portable

step_6_bindings_controllers.adapter: NativeBindings: weva_binding_source over a C# dictionary/list graph or a resolver ({{ path }}, data-class, data-each keyed rows, data-model both ways with the model's types kept, DataChanged); WevaNativeDocument.Bind(model, controller) dispatches on-<event> handler names to controller methods by reflection and refreshes on the next pump when the model moved (RequestRefresh, or a data-model write-back)
step_6_bindings_controllers.frontier_camp: camp_state.gd ported to FrontierCampState/FrontierCampController (Tests/Editor/Native); the example's own camp.html + camp.css drive it through the core: bindings fill the screen (4 keyed rows, derived counts, :disabled from bound attributes), forage -> craft -> place the campfire from its row (TryGetRow key), a disabled button does not reach the controller, the settings dialog writes Player.Name (string), Settings.Volume (int) and Settings.Music (bool) back and the HUD follows, the clock ticks into the masthead
step_6_bindings_controllers.editmode: NativeBindingTests 6/6, FrontierCampNativeTests 5/5 (in the Native run below)

step_7_oracle_from_unity.core_change: ABI minor 26: weva_document_layout_dump serves weva_dump's JSON from the document's box tree (the tool's walk moved into libweva/src/layout_dump.cpp and shared; weva_dump output verified byte-identical on 3 pages after the move) and weva_document_set_font_leading_rounding lets a synthetic face keep fractional half-leading (C ABI test test_abi_layout_dump_and_leading; core suite 505,247 checks, 0 failures; Godot extension builds unchanged)
step_7_oracle_from_unity.unity_side: SyntheticFontBackend (the oracle's face: 0.45em/0.6em advances, 0.85/0.293/1.143em lines, emoji allowlist as MonoFontMetrics, leading rounding off), NativeLayoutDump, the manifest-driven EditMode dump, hosts/unity/oracle_from_unity.py comparing with run_oracle.py's compare()
step_7_oracle_from_unity.first_attempt: an element-level dump through the C ABI agreed on 20/47: box-tree depth (line and anonymous boxes count a level), box order within a line, transform translation and the ABI font path's leading rounding were all adapter differences, which is why the dump moved into the core
step_7_oracle_from_unity.differences_explained: all five remaining pages are CSS animations: weva_dump lays out with no animation clock (base styles), the hosted document applies keyframes at time 0 (an entrance animation's from-state, a mote's start position); docs/ORACLE.md already lists animated values as what the oracle cannot arbitrate. Not an adapter difference: every static page agrees exactly at four decimals.
step_7_oracle_from_unity.gate: met for every non-animated page (42/42); the 5 animated pages differ by the animation clock, not the host
